summary: Postgres database became unavailable or refused connections, causing inventory and orders services to fail all database queries, exhaust connection pools, and propagate errors up to the gateway.

leads: Check `http_server_requests_seconds_count{outcome="SERVER_ERROR"}` for inventory and orders to see which requests are failing. (runbook:triage-high-error-rate)
Check gateway logs for upstream request failures or timeouts to identify which backend service is not answering. (runbook:gateway-upstream)
Check if caller outgoing call latency rises alongside server latency and whether connection pools are exhausted. (runbook:triage-high-latency)
triage.query: HighErrorRate gateway gateway: 63.51% of requests are failing; HighErrorRate inventory inventory: 63.64% of requests are failing; HighErrorRate orders orders: 63.95% of requests are failing

related.text:
- An alert like "orders: 12% of requests are failing".
- `http_server_requests_seconds_count{outcome="SERVER_ERROR"}` rising for one or
  more services.
- Callers log failed calls. The gateway logs "upstream request failed" (502) or
  "upstream request timed out" (504).
related.title: HighErrorRate: a service is returning 5xx

related.text:
The gateway proxies `/api` requests to orders and inventory, with one upstream
timeout for all routes (`UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS`, normally 4000 ms). It answers 502
"upstream request failed" when it can't reach an upstream, and 504 "upstream
request timed out" when the upstream doesn't answer in time. It logs every
failure with the timeout and the error.
related.title: Gateway 502 and 504 responses

related.text:
- An alert like "orders: p95 latency is 2.3s".
- Callers' outgoing call latency (`http_client_requests_seconds`) rises together
  with the callee's server latency.
- Once latency passes a caller's timeout it turns into errors: the gateway
  returns 504 "upstream request timed out", and HikariCP logs "Connection is not
  available, request timed out after 2000ms".
related.title: HighLatency: p95 above one second

triage.summary: High error rates are affecting gateway, inventory, and orders services, causing failures for users trying to place requests.

hypotheses.summary: Postgres is unavailable or refusing connections, causing inventory and orders to fail database operations, saturate connection pools, and return errors to the gateway.

evidence.quote: Caused by: org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: Connection to postgres:5432 refused. Check that the hostname and port are correct and that the postmaster is accepting TCP/IP connections.
evidence.shows: Inventory service cannot connect to the database because postgres refuses connections or is unavailable.
Inventory DB connection pool is exhausted waiting for connections to postgres.

evidence.quote: Caused by: org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: Connection to postgres:5432 refused.
evidence.shows: Orders service also encounters connection refused errors when attempting to connect to postgres.

hypotheses.suggested_fix: Check postgres container/pod health, ensure the database server is running and accepting TCP/IP connections on port 5432, and check network policies or service endpoints.

review.reason: The evidence clearly shows both inventory and orders services failing to connect to postgres:5432 with connection refused errors, leading to connection pool saturation and high error rates across dependent services.
